title: Tailplane Attachment Fitting Interface Standard and Wear Coating Change
abstract: Proposes a revised mating face standard and a harder wear coating at the tailplane attachment fittings, after early fretting and coating breakdown was found at the first heavy checks on high utilisation aircraft.

sections.reason: Two aircraft from one high utilisation operator, both running about eleven cycles a week, showed bright fretting on the attachment fitting mating faces and coating loss around two fitting bores at their first heavy check. Nothing was cracked and nothing was outside limits, but the condition appeared at roughly half the interval the maintenance programme assumes, and the refurbishment added three shifts to each check. A third aircraft from the same operator is due in the shop next spring and will confirm whether this is utilisation driven or fleet wide.
sections.description: The proposal changes the mating face preparation at the fitting interface to a controlled roughness with a harder wear coating, and replaces the obsolete aft fitting with the current kit item so that the coating can be applied at build rather than in the shop. The gusset at the upper attachment is replaced by a variant with a larger bearing face that spreads the load away from the bore edge where the coating breaks down first. Anchor nuts at the interface are brought to the current standard. The attachment geometry and the pin sizes are unchanged, so the stabiliser remains interchangeable between airframes.
sections.effects: Mass increase of two point eight kilograms at the empennage. No electrical load change. Interchangeable at assembly level. The main effect is on the maintenance programme rather than on the aircraft: if the coating performs, the refurbishment task at heavy check can be reduced to an inspection, which is the outcome the operator has asked for. The structure repair manual limits at the fitting bore and the attachment inspection task both require reissue.
sections.embodiment_note: Proposed for production cut-in and for embodiment at a stabiliser overhaul; there is no line retrofit because the mating faces are only accessible with the stabiliser off.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must establish whether the harder coating is compatible with the existing corrosion protection scheme at the bore, whether the larger gusset bearing face fits inside the empennage harness routing that runs across the same fitting, and whether the inspection relief the operator wants can be justified before in-service coating data exists.

type_data.balance_impact: Small aft shift, inside the loading manual tolerance
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in proposed once the coating qualification closes; shop process change at the empennage station
